label: Internal AI tool launch — execution + second-order risk
input: We're rolling out an AI meeting summarizer to all 1,200 employees next month. It integrates with Zoom and Google Calendar. Legal has approved it. The goal is to cut post-meeting documentation time by 50%.
expected_behaviors: Uses past tense throughout — 'it failed because' not 'it might fail because'
Sets a specific future date, not 'in the future'
Identifies a failure chain with at least 3 linked steps — not a flat list
Names second-order failure type as a candidate (tool works → surfaces a new problem)
Kill shots are specific to THIS tool — not generic 'adoption was low'
Early warning signals are observable without special tooling
30/60/90 day signals exist for each kill shot
'What to change now' is a pre-launch action, not a monitoring plan
Does NOT contain trendslop like 'in today's AI landscape'
disqualifying_behaviors: Uses future tense ('this might fail', 'could cause issues')
Kill shots are generic (budget, leadership, adoption) without specific mechanisms
No failure chain — just a list of risks
Early warning signals require building new instrumentation to detect
Omits the 'What to change now' section

label: External AI product launch — assumption failure dominance
input: We're launching an AI-powered expense reporting tool for finance teams at mid-market companies (200–2000 employees). It auto-categorizes receipts, flags policy violations, and drafts exception requests. Pricing is $8/user/month. We go live in 10 weeks with 3 design partners. Target: 50 paying customers in 6 months.
expected_behaviors: Identifies assumption failure as primary type (buyer, workflow, willingness-to-pay assumptions)
Failure chain traces from a specific wrong assumption to a terminal event
Kill shot #1 is specific to finance/expense domain — not generic SaaS failure
Flags concentration risk on 3 design partners shaping a 50-customer target
Second-order kill shot candidate: design partners are outliers, not representative of real ICP
Early warning: 30-day signal detectable from design partner behavior before broad launch
'What to change now' includes at least one change to the design partner selection or process
disqualifying_behaviors: Future tense anywhere in the output
Kill shots don't reference the finance/expense domain specifically
No signal for the design-partner assumption risk
Generic 'competition' kill shot without naming a specific competitor or mechanism
